education is a primary way that wealth is transferred from one generation to another, that this intergenerational transmission of wealth is not equally distributed among the population and that this unequal distribution is likely to reduce the social mobility of our society.

(1) education is a major means of intergenerational transmission of wealth in the United States, (2) the lack of access to quality education for those who cannot afford it is a major barrier to social mobility, and (3) public investment in education is declining and being replaced by private investment, which is a form of indirect intergenerational wealth transfer.
